newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER UNITED MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LIVERPOOL V MANCHESTER UNITED MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Liverpool and Manchester United who meet in the English premier league at Anfield on Saturday (kick-off 1015 GMT)

Playing style: Roy Evans favours a fluid 3-5-2 formation with an emphasis on solid defence and quick counter-attacks in the traditional Liverpool style. Evans's Liverpool, unlike that of his predecessor Graeme Souness, also display the quick, short, sharp passing game and hard running off the ball, a Liverpool hallmark since the 1960s. Jamie Redknapp, Steve McManaman and Jason McAteer link between defence and attack providing the ammunition for Robbie Fowler and either Stan Collymore or Patrick Berger up front.

Strengths: The finishing of Fowler, the incisive running of McManaman, the overall confidence of the team. Liverpool have wonderfully talented players in every position and have never lost the capability of pressuring opponents for long periods until they crack.

Weaknesses: The current poor form of goalkeeper David James is undermining Liverpool's game. An over-elaboration with their passing game sometimes causes them to lose the initiative. James needs to be at his best, and Liverpool at their most incisive to get all three points against United on Saturday.

Motivation: With the probable outcome of the title at stake on this match, Liverpool have all the motivation they need. They will also be keen to avenge last season's FA Cup final defeat and the 1-0 defeat at Old Trafford in October, which brought to a close their unbeaten start to this season. The row between the clubs over extending the season should also add some extra spice to an already hot and heated occasion.

Playing style: Manchester United's playing-style has been based on a quick counter-attacking game for years. Manager Alex Ferguson, 55, has so many players at his disposal he can vary his tactics and formations with relative ease, but generally United play with four men across the back and the rest buzzing around creating havoc in midfield and attack. Eric Cantona holds the attacking unit of the team together while David Beckham's industrious runs and long-range shooting this season have given United an even greater range of options coming forward.

Strengths: An outstanding team spirit and the size of the squad means that if one player is injured, another can usually step into the vacant position with a seemingly invisible transition. The speed at which United can turn from defence to attack is also another big advantage.

Weaknesses: If United do have a weakness going into the match it is likely to be in defence with goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel, and defenders David May and Denis Irwin doubtful. Overall, United's only weakness is the occasional loss of form or concentration that can hit any team at any time.

Motivation: Victory at Anfield would not guarantee United the title, but would make it much harder for anyone else to win it and probably end Liverpool's hopes at the same time. Ferguson's well-publicised row with Roy Evans over extending the season should also give him greater incentive than usual to send his team out to victory.
